teaser: A key makes a browser an editor's: reads, sign-offs and fixes go to a vault, a daily pass acts and replies, and five lanes set what any reader sends.
core_idea: Editing from a chat loses the page, the version and the sentence; an editor key turns a browser into an editor's, which sends a subset of its reading to an editor vault, a daily pass acts on what is cheap to undo and replies, and five audiences each get a lane and a key, moving from shared secrets to key pairs.

nodes.label: The lane goes one way

nodes.label: The editor vault

nodes.label: Signed off
nodes.summary: Against a version; stale when it changes.

nodes.label: The daily pass
nodes.summary: Checks, cheap fixes released, the rest proposed.

nodes.label: Cheap to undo
nodes.summary: Articles are two-way doors; email is not.

nodes.label: Key pairs
nodes.summary: Sign, seal, grant and revoke per person.

nodes.label: The brief
nodes.summary: For the agent that builds the pane.

quotes.text: Without the key, the code that does any of this never runs.
The agent can then say, for every article, whether the version that is live is the version I signed off.
